subject: Re: ACME Robotics — technical qualification & SDK fit
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sydney Park <sydney@acmerobotics.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 16:00:00 -0800
Subject: ACME Robotics — technical qualification & SDK fit

Hi Sydney & Kevin,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciated the candid walkthrough of the current workflow. Below is a concise recap from our side to make sure we’re aligned on pain, goals, and immediate next steps. We’ll hold off on pricing until after the technical deep-dive, but wanted to capture product fit notes that will shape the proposal.

Key pain points you emphasized:
- Search relevance drops for multi-turn queries; existing reranker is brittle with contextual prompts.
- High cost per query when using server-side embeddings + complex retrieval every request.
- Latency spikes during peak telemetry ingestion, impacting the operator UI (95th p99 threshold).

Goals discussed:
1) Improve precision for multi-turn assistance (reduce false positives in rerank).
2) Lower per-query unit cost via prefix caching + batched embeddings.
3) Smooth UI experience with streaming partial responses for progressive display and token-level latency SLOs.

Integration & product fit summary (technical):
- SDK / client changes: we recommend using Redwood’s 1.4+ JS SDK (we’ll share the guide) — it exposes streaming hooks and an easy embedding-batch helper.
- Function calling: good fit for tool orchestration you described (query-store lookups, generate->validate pipelines). We can map your tool schema to Redwood function signatures; function-calls can return structured JSON that our runtime validates before returning.
- Streaming: Redwood streaming supports incremental JSON chunks (application/ndjson style) and a token-level backpressure callback so your UI can show partial structured outputs without rehydrating the whole response.
- Structured outputs: we can enforce a JSON schema on model responses (e.g., {action, payload,score}) to make downstream rerank deterministic.
- Embeddings & reranking: recommend switching to a hybrid approach — dense embeddings for candidate retrieval with a learned lightweight reranker on top (we can supply an embeddings pipeline and eval harness).

Immediate next steps (owner / timeline):
- Action: Schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with your infra + search engineer and our solutions engineer (Vivek). Owner: Karthik / Sydney. Target: next week.
- Action: Sydney to share a sanitized sample of your payloads (prompt examples + small subset of retrieval logs, ~500 rows). Owner: Sydney. Target: before deep-dive.
- Action: Redwood to send SDK integration guide + a short SOW stub covering a pilot (data ingestion, 2-week eval harness, one dedicated model tuning pass). Owner: Karthik. Target: within 48 hours.

Attachments: I’ve attached a short SDK integration guide and a 1-page pilot SOW draft for your review.

If anything above is off, flag it and I’ll update. Otherwise I’ll propose two times for the deep-dive tomorrow morning.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0114

Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 17:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Robotics — technical qualification & SDK fit

Thanks Karthik — this is exactly the kind of framing we wanted. A few clarifications from our side:

- Priority: multi-turn rerank quality > latency > cost (in that order). If we can get reliable rerank improvements for the top-5 candidates, that’s a win.
- Current stack: our retriever is an in-house vector store built on Faiss; embeddings are generated offline in a nightly batch. We’d like to move to on-demand smaller-batch embeddings for freshness, but cost is a constraint.
- Streaming: we absolutely need streaming for the operator UI. If Redwood can provide incremental tokens plus a JSON chunking approach for partial structured outputs, that’ll match our UI design.

I’ll share a redacted CSV of example queries + retrieval context (about 300 rows) and a short doc describing our reranker heuristics — expect that by EOD Monday.

One technical ask up front: do you have an example of how function-calling maps to external tool invocations (signature + sample JSON exchange)? If you can drop that in the SDK guide it’ll accelerate our internal mapping.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

—Sydney
Head of ML Infrastructure | ACME Robotics
sydney@acmerobotics.com

Attachments: acme-llm-requirements.xlsx (XLSX, 180KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sydney Park <sydney@acmerobotics.com>, Kevin Liu <kevin@acmerobotics.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME Robotics — technical qualification & SDK fit

Appreciate the quick turnaround, Sydney. A few concrete notes addressing your asks and proposed slots for next week.

1) Function-calling example (high level):
- Signature: function name + typed params (JSON schema). Example call: "/functions/lookup_customer" -> payload: {"customer_id": "string", "context": [..]}.
- Our runtime: executes function-call hooks server-side, returns structured JSON to the SDK; you can opt to run functions in your infra (we forward a webhook) or use Redwood-hosted connectors.
- We’ll include a complete example in the SDK guide showing a generate -> function-call -> validate -> rerank flow.

2) Streaming behavior:
- Streaming response is an NDJSON stream of objects: {"type": "chunk", "partial": "text"} and {"type": "structured", "value": {...}} for schema-confirmed payloads. There’s a backpressure callback in the JS SDK so your UI can pause/resume.

3) Embeddings & rerank approach:
- Pilot plan: run an A/B on a small subset with (a) nightly batch embeddings (current) vs (b) on-demand mini-batches + prefix cache. We'll provide the evaluation harness — metric targets: MAP@5 and p95 latency.

4) Scheduling: proposed deep-dive slots (PST):
- Tue 24 Feb, 10:00–11:00
- Wed 25 Feb, 14:00–15:00

Action items captured:
- Karthik: send SDK guide + function-calling example + SOW stub (sent earlier; will reattach).
- Sydney: share redacted payloads + reranker doc (EOD Mon).
- Vivek: lead the deep-dive (technical).

We’ll also include a short eval checklist (what sample queries to provide, desired success metrics). If those slots work I’ll lock and send a calendar invite with a brief agenda.

Best,
Karthik

Attachments: redwood-sdkintegration-guide.pdf (updated, 1.2MB), acme-proto-sow-draft.docx

- Pricing posture: propose a 6-week paid pilot at $18k with a 30% credit toward a committed Dedicated contract if they convert within 90 days. This is preliminary — we’ll refine after the deep-dive.
